tasks.gr10-matter-states-phase-change-t2: Grade 10 Physical Sciences Term 2: States of matter, kinetic molecular theory, and phase changes.
tasks.gr10-atoms-periodic-table-bonding-t2: Grade 10 Physical Sciences Term 2: Atomic structure, the periodic table trends, and chemical bonding (ionic and covalent).
tasks.gr10-magnetism-t2: Topic: Magnetism. Cover the poles of a permanent magnet (like poles repel, unlike poles attract, poles cannot be separated), the magnetic field and field lines (from north to south outside the magnet, closer lines mean a stronger field, lines never cross), the compass needle, the Earth's magnetic field (a magnetic south pole near the geographic North Pole, so a compass points north), magnetic materials (iron, cobalt, nickel, steel) and that only repulsion proves that an object is a magnet. Ask Grade 10 learners to predict forces, read field directions and choose materials.
tasks.gr10-particles-substances-t2: Topic: Particles substances are made of. Cover atoms and molecules, reading formulae and counting atoms (H₂SO₄ has 7 atoms, Ca(OH)₂ has 5), molecular, ionic and metallic substances, and how the particles decide the properties: molecular substances have low melting points and do not conduct; ionic solids have high melting points, are brittle and conduct only when molten or dissolved; metals conduct as solids because of free electrons and can be hammered into shape. Ask Grade 10 learners to count atoms, classify substances and explain conductivity and melting points.
tasks.gr10-physical-chemical-change-t2: Topic: Physical and chemical change. Cover physical change (no new substance: melting, boiling, dissolving) and chemical change (a new substance), evidence of chemical change, the law of conservation of mass and atoms with balanced equations (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO: 48 g + 32 g = 80 g; use relative atomic masses Mg = 24, O = 16, Ca = 40, C = 12 and quote them), and exothermic (energy released) and endothermic (energy absorbed) reactions. Ask Grade 10 learners to classify changes, check mass conservation and identify energy changes.
tasks.gr10-electrostatics-basics-t2: Topic: Electrostatics basics. Cover two kinds of charge, like charges repel and unlike attract, neutral objects, charging by friction as a transfer of electrons only, conductors and insulators, conservation of charge (identical spheres that touch share the total charge equally) and quantisation Q = n e with e = 1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (quote it in each question that needs it). Do not use Coulomb's law (Grade 11). Ask Grade 10 learners to decide forces, who gains electrons, and to calculate charge and electron numbers.
